problem.statement:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the index of target if it exists in the array. If the target is not found, return -1.

Solve using linear search (check each element from left to right).

examples.explanation: 6 does not exist in the array.

hints: If you finish the loop, return -1.

sections.title: Intuition
sections.content:
The naive way is to think of checking each element one by one from left to right.
Keep comparing each element with the target until we find a match or reach the end of the array.

sections.title: Approach
sections.content:
• Traverse through the array, similar to the idea of scanning each element serially.
• Check if the current element of array is equal to the target element.
• If so, return the index and stop scanning further.
• In case the target value is not found, return -1 marking that the target element is missing.

solutions.python:
def linear_search(nums, target):
    # Traverse the array
    for i in range(len(nums)):
        # Check if current element is target
        if nums[i] == target:
            return i
    # If target not found
    return -1

# Example usage
arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print(linear_search(arr, 3))

editorial.timeComplexity: O(N), in worst case the entire array will be traversed, taking time N where N is the size of the array.
editorial.spaceComplexity: O(1), no extra space is used apart from the input array.
